G.notes: verl's own trainer owns the loop: verl.trainer.main_ppo -> RayPPOTrainer.fit(). smoke25 (2026-09-11) ran one complete GRPO step: 16 real Pi episodes certified -> advantages -> update_actor 117.6s -> update_weights 2.98s -> global_step_1; P1 adapter sha256 f0ddcac8... differs from frozen P0 6db6a40c..., so the update is real. 5.3 item 2 upgraded. smoke27 (n=32, total_epochs=2, max_attempts=3, 22m34s) then ran TWO steps and closed item 9: generation 0 rolled out under P0 (adapter_revision 6db6a40c..., episode fingerprint e3eca6fe...), its first draw was refused as a degenerate batch and redrawn (rejected-attempt0.json), the redraw certified, step 1 synced in place (2.90s) and wrote global_step_1; generation 1 then rolled out under policy_generation P1 with adapter_revision 13cc8199..., which is the recomputed digest of global_step_1/actor (MATCH), episode fingerprint aed2a953..., and step 2 produced a different adapter (30e3f3ad...) from it. The engine still cannot self-report its step (checkpoint_engine.backend=naive discards global_steps), so policy identity is bound by the digest of the checkpoint the framework itself wrote, and the gap is recorded per call. All 13 acceptance items are therefore satisfied and the 5.4 claim is enabled. No learning improvement is claimed: 2/32 then 1/32 solves is noise.
